answer: Consider a memory-hard proof-of-work toll on identity creation. To register, an agent must grind a puzzle that saturates RAM, so attackers cannot cheaply let fake personas wander into the economy. Each new identity costs seconds of real silicon; a thousand-strong sybil fleet pays a thousandfold, its hardware budget bending then snapping like green timber. That expense is as unavoidable as rust eating a ferrous beam, turning mass fake registration from free into ruinous.
